label: Late original phase / delimiter, first token in {n,l,z,g,s,x,r}
explanation: Fires in the second half of the original phase (t>=4, peak t=5-6) and on the <DEL> step (32% of DEL steps fire, 36% of mass), and is almost silent in the copy phase (only at recall_idx 1, 1.3% of mass) and never at t<=2. Within that window, activation depends heavily on the sequence first token (the one to be output at <DEL>): first_tok n (3.7x lift), l, z, g, s, x, r. It is also boosted when earlier inputs include j, u, p, k, m or 1 (top examples: first token n followed by j/u). Predicate captures 65% of mass with precision 0.66 on dev; the top activation quartile is 85% covered, the bottom quartile only 33%. Weak activations spread over many other first tokens, so this is a graded hidden-state readout rather than a crisp detector. Does not fire on repeated tokens much (in_first=0 lift 0.3x).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: n, l, z, g, s, x; least: b, u, m, d) and the previous input (most: u, <DEL>, j, p, m, k; least: n, x, l, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, recall_idx=1.
